stem: Out of the following which is the Pythagorean triplet?
solution: A Pythagorean triplet \((a, b, c)\) satisfies \(a^2 + b^2 = c^2\). For \((3, 4, 5)\): \(3^2 + 4^2 = 9 + 16 = 25 = 5^2\). \(\therefore (3, 4, 5)\) is a Pythagorean triplet.

stem: Two circles having radii \(4\) cm and \(5\) cm touch each other internally. Then the distance between the centres is ________.
solution: When two circles touch each other internally, the distance between their centres equals the difference of their radii. \(\therefore d = 5 - 4 = 1\) cm.

stem: Out of the following points ________ lies to the right of the origin on X-axis.
solution: A point on the X-axis has y-coordinate \(0\); it lies to the right of the origin when its x-coordinate is positive. Only \((2, 0)\) has \(y = 0\) and \(x = 2 > 0\). \(\therefore\) the point is \((2, 0)\).

subtopic: Surface Area and Volume of Solids
stem: If the side of the cube is \(5\) cm, then the volume of that cube is ________.
solution: Volume of a cube \(= (\text{side})^3 = 5^3 = 125\) cm\(^3\).

subtopic: Theorem of Areas of Similar Triangles
stem: The ratio of corresponding sides of similar triangles is \(3 : 5\), then find the ratio of their areas.
solution: The ratio of the areas of two similar triangles equals the ratio of the squares of their corresponding sides. \(\therefore \dfrac{A(\triangle_1)}{A(\triangle_2)} = \left(\dfrac{3}{5}\right)^2 = \dfrac{9}{25}\). Hence the ratio of their areas is \(9 : 25\).

stem: Find the side of a square if its diagonal is \(10\sqrt{2}\) cm.
solution: For a square of side \(a\), the diagonal \(d = a\sqrt{2}\). \(\therefore a\sqrt{2} = 10\sqrt{2} \Rightarrow a = 10\) cm. Hence the side of the square is \(10\) cm.

stem: If the measure of minor arc is \(70^\circ\), then find the measure of the corresponding major arc.
solution: The measures of the minor arc and its corresponding major arc add up to \(360^\circ\). \(\therefore\) measure of major arc \(= 360^\circ - 70^\circ = 290^\circ\).

stem: Angle made by the line with the positive direction of X-axis is \(45^\circ\), find the slope of the line.
solution: Slope \(= \tan\theta = \tan 45^\circ = 1\).

subtopic: Tangent and Secant to a Circle
stem: In the following figure, seg PS is a tangent segment and line PR is a secant. If \(PQ = 3.6\), \(QR = 6.4\), complete the activity to find PS.
solution: By the tangent secant segment theorem, \(PS^2 = PQ \times PR\). Now \(PR = PQ + QR = 3.6 + 6.4 = 10\). \(\therefore PS^2 = PQ \times (PQ + QR) = 3.6 \times 10 = 36\). \(\therefore PS = \sqrt{36} = 6\).
figureNote: circle with external point P; seg PS tangent to circle at S; secant line PR through the circle meeting it at Q and R (P-Q-R), p-03

stem: If \(\sec\theta = \dfrac{25}{7}\), complete the activity to find the value of \(\tan\theta\).
solution: Using the identity \(1 + \tan^2\theta = \sec^2\theta\): \(1 + \tan^2\theta = \left(\dfrac{25}{7}\right)^2 = \dfrac{625}{49}\). \(\therefore \tan^2\theta = \dfrac{625}{49} - 1 = \dfrac{625 - 49}{49} = \dfrac{576}{49}\). \(\therefore \tan\theta = \sqrt{\dfrac{576}{49}} = \dfrac{24}{7}\).

stem: In the following figure, side of square ABCD is \(7\) cm. With centre D and radius DA, sector D-AXC is drawn. Complete the activity to find the area of the shaded region. (Area of sector \(D\text{-}AXC = 38.5\) cm\(^2\).)
solution: Area of square \(= (\text{side})^2 = 7^2 = 49\) cm\(^2\). The shaded region is the part of the square outside the sector. \(\therefore A(\text{shaded region}) = A(\text{square ABCD}) - A(\text{sector D-AXC}) = 49 - 38.5 = 10.5\) cm\(^2\).
figureNote: square ABCD of side 7 cm (A top-left, D top-right, C bottom-right, B bottom-left); quarter-circle sector D-AXC with centre D and radius DA, arc AXC through X inside the square; region of square outside the sector is shaded, p-04

stem: Find QP using the given information in the figure. (In \(\triangle MNP\), Q lies on side MP, seg NQ bisects \(\angle MNP\), \(MN = 25\), \(MQ = 14\), \(NP = 40\).)
solution: In \(\triangle MNP\), seg NQ is the bisector of \(\angle MNP\) with Q on MP. By the property of the angle bisector of a triangle, \(\dfrac{MQ}{QP} = \dfrac{MN}{NP}\). \(\therefore \dfrac{14}{QP} = \dfrac{25}{40} \Rightarrow QP = \dfrac{14 \times 40}{25} = \dfrac{560}{25} = 22.4\).
figureNote: triangle MNP (M top, N bottom-left, P bottom-right); Q on side MP with MQ=14 marked and MN=25, NP=40; seg NQ drawn bisecting angle N (double arc marks at N), p-05

stem: In \(\triangle RST\), \(\angle S = 90^\circ\), \(\angle T = 30^\circ\), \(RT = 12\) cm, then find RS and ST.
solution: In \(\triangle RST\), \(\angle S = 90^\circ\), so RT is the hypotenuse. \(\angle T = 30^\circ\) and \(\angle R = 60^\circ\), so it is a \(30^\circ\text{–}60^\circ\text{–}90^\circ\) triangle. The side opposite \(30^\circ\) is half the hypotenuse: \(RS = \dfrac{1}{2} \times RT = \dfrac{1}{2} \times 12 = 6\) cm. The side opposite \(60^\circ\) is \(\dfrac{\sqrt{3}}{2}\) times the hypotenuse: \(ST = \dfrac{\sqrt{3}}{2} \times 12 = 6\sqrt{3}\) cm.

stem: In the following figure, chord MN and chord RS intersect at point D. If \(RD = 15\), \(DS = 4\), \(MD = 8\), find DN.
solution: By the theorem of internal division of two chords, if two chords of a circle intersect inside the circle then the products of the two parts of each chord are equal: \(MD \times DN = RD \times DS\). \(\therefore 8 \times DN = 15 \times 4 = 60 \Rightarrow DN = \dfrac{60}{8} = 7.5\).
figureNote: circle with two chords MN and RS intersecting at interior point D; M and S near top, R bottom-left, N right; RD=15, DS=4, MD=8 marked, p-06

stem: Find the co-ordinates of the midpoint of the line segment joining the points \(P(0, 6)\) and \(Q(12, 20)\).
solution: Midpoint \(= \left(\dfrac{x_1 + x_2}{2}, \dfrac{y_1 + y_2}{2}\right) = \left(\dfrac{0 + 12}{2}, \dfrac{6 + 20}{2}\right) = \left(\dfrac{12}{2}, \dfrac{26}{2}\right) = (6, 13)\).

stem: Prove that: \(\sin^2\theta + \cos^2\theta = 1\).
solution: Consider a right-angled triangle with acute angle \(\theta\), opposite side \(p\), adjacent side \(b\) and hypotenuse \(h\). Then \(\sin\theta = \dfrac{p}{h}\) and \(\cos\theta = \dfrac{b}{h}\). \(\therefore \sin^2\theta + \cos^2\theta = \dfrac{p^2}{h^2} + \dfrac{b^2}{h^2} = \dfrac{p^2 + b^2}{h^2}\). By the Pythagoras theorem, \(p^2 + b^2 = h^2\). \(\therefore \sin^2\theta + \cos^2\theta = \dfrac{h^2}{h^2} = 1\). Hence proved.

stem: In the following figure, seg XY \(\parallel\) side AC. If \(2AX = 3BX\) and \(XY = 9\), complete the activity to find the value of AC.
solution: \(2AX = 3BX \Rightarrow \dfrac{AX}{BX} = \dfrac{3}{2}\). By componendo, \(\dfrac{AX + BX}{BX} = \dfrac{3 + 2}{2}\), i.e. \(\dfrac{AB}{BX} = \dfrac{5}{2}\). Since seg XY \(\parallel\) side AC, \(\triangle BCA \sim \triangle BYX\) (AA test of similarity). \(\therefore \dfrac{BA}{BX} = \dfrac{AC}{XY}\) (corresponding sides of similar triangles). \(\therefore \dfrac{5}{2} = \dfrac{AC}{9} \Rightarrow AC = \dfrac{5 \times 9}{2} = \dfrac{45}{2} = 22.5\).
figureNote: triangle ABC (A top, B bottom-left, C bottom-right); X on side AB and Y on side BC with seg XY parallel to side AC, p-06

stem: For finding AB and BC with the help of the information given in the following figure, complete the following activity. (In \(\triangle ABC\), \(\angle B = 90^\circ\), \(AB = BC\) and hypotenuse \(AC = \sqrt{8}\).)
solution: In \(\triangle ABC\), \(\angle B = 90^\circ\) and \(AB = BC\), so it is an isosceles right-angled triangle. Since the two legs are equal, the base angles are equal: \(\angle BAC = \angle BCA = 45^\circ\). In a \(45^\circ\text{–}45^\circ\text{–}90^\circ\) triangle, each leg \(= \dfrac{1}{\sqrt{2}} \times\) hypotenuse. \(\therefore AB = BC = \dfrac{1}{\sqrt{2}} \times AC = \dfrac{1}{\sqrt{2}} \times \sqrt{8} = \dfrac{1}{\sqrt{2}} \times 2\sqrt{2} = 2\). Hence \(AB = BC = 2\).
figureNote: right-angled triangle ABC (A top, B bottom-left, C bottom-right); right angle at B; legs AB and BC marked equal (tick marks); hypotenuse AC labelled sqrt(8), p-07

stem: Prove that: The tangent segments drawn from an external point to the circle are congruent.
solution: Given: A circle with centre O. P is a point outside the circle. seg PA and seg PB are tangent segments touching the circle at A and B. To prove: \(PA = PB\). Construction: Draw seg OA, seg OB and seg OP. Proof: seg OA and seg OB are radii, and a tangent is perpendicular to the radius at the point of contact, so \(\angle OAP = \angle OBP = 90^\circ\). In right-angled \(\triangle OAP\) and \(\triangle OBP\): hypotenuse \(OP = OP\) (common), \(OA = OB\) (radii of the same circle). \(\therefore \triangle OAP \cong \triangle OBP\) (Hypotenuse-side test). \(\therefore PA = PB\) (corresponding sides of congruent triangles). Hence the tangent segments drawn from an external point to a circle are congruent.

subtopic: Construction of a Tangent to a Circle
stem: Draw a circle with centre O and radius \(3.5\) cm, take a point P at a distance \(5.7\) cm from the centre. Draw tangents to the circle from point P.
solution: Steps of construction: (1) Draw a circle with centre O and radius \(3.5\) cm. (2) Take point P such that \(OP = 5.7\) cm and draw seg OP. (3) Draw the perpendicular bisector of seg OP; let it meet OP at its midpoint M. (4) With centre M and radius \(MO = MP = 2.85\) cm, draw a circle intersecting the given circle at points A and B. (5) Draw lines PA and PB. Then line PA and line PB are the required tangents to the circle from point P. (Verification: since \(OA = 3.5\) and \(OP = 5.7\), \(PA = PB = \sqrt{OP^2 - OA^2} = \sqrt{5.7^2 - 3.5^2} = \sqrt{32.49 - 12.25} = \sqrt{20.24} \approx 4.5\) cm.)

stem: Find the co-ordinates of point P, if P divides the line segment joining the points \(A(-1, 7)\) and \(B(4, -3)\) in the ratio \(2 : 3\).
solution: By the section formula, for P dividing AB in ratio \(m : n = 2 : 3\): \(P = \left(\dfrac{m x_2 + n x_1}{m + n}, \dfrac{m y_2 + n y_1}{m + n}\right)\). \(x = \dfrac{2(4) + 3(-1)}{2 + 3} = \dfrac{8 - 3}{5} = \dfrac{5}{5} = 1\). \(y = \dfrac{2(-3) + 3(7)}{2 + 3} = \dfrac{-6 + 21}{5} = \dfrac{15}{5} = 3\). \(\therefore P = (1, 3)\).

stem: A bucket is frustum shaped. Its height is \(28\) cm. Radii of circular faces are \(12\) cm and \(15\) cm. Find the capacity of the bucket in litres. \(\left(\pi = \dfrac{22}{7}\right)\)
solution: Capacity \(=\) volume of the frustum \(= \dfrac{1}{3}\pi h (R^2 + r^2 + Rr)\), where \(R = 15\), \(r = 12\), \(h = 28\). \(R^2 + r^2 + Rr = 225 + 144 + 180 = 549\). \(V = \dfrac{1}{3} \times \dfrac{22}{7} \times 28 \times 549 = \dfrac{1}{3} \times 88 \times 549 = 88 \times 183 = 16104\) cm\(^3\). Since \(1000\) cm\(^3 = 1\) litre, capacity \(= \dfrac{16104}{1000} = 16.104\) litres.

stem: \(\triangle ABC \sim \triangle ADE\). In \(\triangle ABC\), \(AB = 6.3\) cm, \(\angle CAB = 50^\circ\), \(AC = 5.6\) cm and \(\dfrac{AB}{AD} = \dfrac{7}{5}\). Construct \(\triangle ADE\).
solution: Since \(\triangle ABC \sim \triangle ADE\) with scale factor \(\dfrac{AD}{AB} = \dfrac{5}{7}\), the corresponding sides of \(\triangle ADE\) are: \(AD = \dfrac{5}{7} \times AB = \dfrac{5}{7} \times 6.3 = 4.5\) cm, \(AE = \dfrac{5}{7} \times AC = \dfrac{5}{7} \times 5.6 = 4.0\) cm, and \(\angle DAE = \angle CAB = 50^\circ\). Steps of construction: (1) First construct \(\triangle ABC\) with \(AB = 6.3\) cm, \(\angle CAB = 50^\circ\), \(AC = 5.6\) cm. (2) Since D lies on ray AB (or its side) with \(AD < AB\), mark point D on seg AB such that \(AD = 4.5\) cm. (3) Draw seg DE parallel to seg BC meeting AC at E (then \(AE = 4.0\) cm). (4) \(\triangle ADE\) is the required triangle with \(AD = 4.5\) cm, \(AE = 4.0\) cm, \(\angle DAE = 50^\circ\).

subtopic: Surface Area and Volume of Solids
stem: Surface area of a sphere and total surface area of a cube are same. Show that the ratio of the volume of the sphere to that of the cube is \(\sqrt{6} : \sqrt{\pi}\).
solution: Let the radius of the sphere be \(r\) and the side of the cube be \(a\). Given: surface area of sphere \(=\) total surface area of cube. \(\therefore 4\pi r^2 = 6a^2 \Rightarrow a^2 = \dfrac{2\pi r^2}{3} \Rightarrow a = r\sqrt{\dfrac{2\pi}{3}}\). Now, \(\dfrac{V_{\text{sphere}}}{V_{\text{cube}}} = \dfrac{\frac{4}{3}\pi r^3}{a^3} = \dfrac{\frac{4}{3}\pi r^3}{r^3 \left(\frac{2\pi}{3}\right)^{3/2}}\). Let \(k = \dfrac{2\pi}{3}\); then \(\dfrac{4}{3}\pi = 2k\), so the ratio \(= \dfrac{2k}{k^{3/2}} = \dfrac{2}{\sqrt{k}} = \dfrac{2}{\sqrt{\frac{2\pi}{3}}} = 2\sqrt{\dfrac{3}{2\pi}} = \dfrac{2\sqrt{3}}{\sqrt{2}\,\sqrt{\pi}} = \dfrac{\sqrt{2}\,\sqrt{3}}{\sqrt{\pi}} = \dfrac{\sqrt{6}}{\sqrt{\pi}}\). \(\therefore V_{\text{sphere}} : V_{\text{cube}} = \sqrt{6} : \sqrt{\pi}\). Hence shown.

subtopic: Theorem of Areas of Similar Triangles
stem: In \(\triangle ABC\), A-X-B and A-Y-C is such that segment XY \(\parallel\) side BC. Segment XY divides \(\triangle ABC\) in two equal areas, then find \(\dfrac{BX}{AB}\).
solution: Since seg XY \(\parallel\) side BC, \(\triangle AXY \sim \triangle ABC\). XY divides \(\triangle ABC\) into two equal areas, so \(A(\triangle AXY) = \dfrac{1}{2}A(\triangle ABC)\), i.e. \(\dfrac{A(\triangle AXY)}{A(\triangle ABC)} = \dfrac{1}{2}\). By the theorem of areas of similar triangles, \(\dfrac{A(\triangle AXY)}{A(\triangle ABC)} = \left(\dfrac{AX}{AB}\right)^2\). \(\therefore \left(\dfrac{AX}{AB}\right)^2 = \dfrac{1}{2} \Rightarrow \dfrac{AX}{AB} = \dfrac{1}{\sqrt{2}}\). Now \(\dfrac{BX}{AB} = \dfrac{AB - AX}{AB} = 1 - \dfrac{AX}{AB} = 1 - \dfrac{1}{\sqrt{2}} = \dfrac{\sqrt{2} - 1}{\sqrt{2}} = \dfrac{2 - \sqrt{2}}{2}\).

stem: Seg PQ is a chord of a circle. Arc PXQ is a major arc and arc PYQ is a minor arc. \(\angle POQ\) is the central angle of the circle. (a) Draw the figure from the given information. (b) Find the measure of \(\angle PXQ\), \(\angle PYQ\) and add \(m\angle PXQ,\ m\angle PYQ\). (c) Find the measure of \(\angle POQ\). Write the relation between \(\angle PXQ\) and \(\angle POQ\).
solution: (a) Draw a circle with centre O and a chord PQ. Take point X on the major arc and point Y on the minor arc, and draw radii OP and OQ so that \(\angle POQ\) is the central angle standing on the minor arc PYQ. (b) \(\angle PXQ\) is an inscribed angle in the major arc that intercepts minor arc PYQ, so \(m\angle PXQ = \dfrac{1}{2}\,m(\text{arc PYQ})\). \(\angle PYQ\) is an inscribed angle in the minor arc that intercepts major arc PXQ, so \(m\angle PYQ = \dfrac{1}{2}\,m(\text{arc PXQ})\). Adding, \(m\angle PXQ + m\angle PYQ = \dfrac{1}{2}\big[m(\text{arc PYQ}) + m(\text{arc PXQ})\big] = \dfrac{1}{2} \times 360^\circ = 180^\circ\). (This also follows because PXQY is a cyclic quadrilateral, whose opposite angles are supplementary.) (c) The central angle equals the measure of its intercepted (minor) arc: \(m\angle POQ = m(\text{arc PYQ})\). Since \(m\angle PXQ = \dfrac{1}{2}\,m(\text{arc PYQ})\), the relation is \(m\angle PXQ = \dfrac{1}{2}\,m\angle POQ\), i.e. \(m\angle POQ = 2\,m\angle PXQ\).

stem: Two eagles are flying in the sky at a height of \(10\sqrt{3}\) m above the ground. A boy standing at a point on the ground looks towards the eagles making angles of elevation of \(60^\circ\) and \(30^\circ\) respectively. Find the distance between these two eagles.
solution: Let the boy stand at point P on the ground. Both eagles are at height \(h = 10\sqrt{3}\) m. For the eagle at elevation \(60^\circ\), let its horizontal distance from P be \(d_1\): \(\tan 60^\circ = \dfrac{10\sqrt{3}}{d_1} \Rightarrow \sqrt{3} = \dfrac{10\sqrt{3}}{d_1} \Rightarrow d_1 = 10\) m. For the eagle at elevation \(30^\circ\), horizontal distance \(d_2\): \(\tan 30^\circ = \dfrac{10\sqrt{3}}{d_2} \Rightarrow \dfrac{1}{\sqrt{3}} = \dfrac{10\sqrt{3}}{d_2} \Rightarrow d_2 = 10\sqrt{3} \times \sqrt{3} = 30\) m. As both eagles are at the same height and on the same side, the distance between them equals the difference of the horizontal distances: \(d_2 - d_1 = 30 - 10 = 20\) m.
